miniProject.title: Ordered collectives with a CPU correctness suite
miniProject.brief: Build the rank and group layer in `comm/` and check every collective against a single-process oracle on CPU processes. Exact ordering, ownership and cost reasoning here prevents hangs and silent mismatch in every parallel design that follows.
steps: Launch CPU processes with `torchrun`, map global ranks to devices through the launcher variables, and build the default group plus nested subgroups for a small grid, each run on a distinct port with `gloo`.
Exchange tensors with matched blocking and non-blocking send and receive pairs, then broadcast and reduce; prove which ranks hold valid results and show an early buffer touch corrupts the handoff.

Implement all-reduce, all-gather, reduce-scatter and all-to-all on several CPU processes, checking every rank against single-process oracles; pass the TensorTonic collectives cases and derive the per-rank byte factor for each.

Run the order-swap drill with a short timeout and attribute the hang with `monitored_barrier` and debug output; issue one async collective with compute between issue and wait, reporting CPU timings as issue cost only.

Derive ring and tree all-reduce costs from the latency-bandwidth model and locate the crossover; pass the TensorTonic bandwidth cases and sweep sizes with warmup and synchronization, adding a measured variant only with two or more GPUs while recording backend and link tier beside every number.

Ship the CPU multiprocess collective suite in `tests/` covering ranks, subgroups, dtypes and edges with deterministic seeds; keep rank-attributed logs with collective sequence numbers, bounded teardown, and one injected fault that fails its exact assertion.
deliverables: The `comm/` rank and group layer with launch, mapping and subgroup construction.
The CPU collective suite with oracle comparisons, edge coverage and the injected-fault demonstration.
Cost derivations, the CPU sweep table and rank-attributed logs with teardown evidence.

checks.name: TensorTonic: Simulate Distributed Collectives
checks.note: Pass the gather, scatter and all-to-all cases in your harness before the multiprocess runs.

checks.name: TensorTonic: Calculate Collective Effective Bandwidth
checks.note: Pass the public byte-factor cases; reconcile the table with your sweep knee.

rubric.pass: Every collective matches the single-process oracle on every rank across subgroups, dtypes and edge cases.
rubric.strong: An uneven-split case and a subgroup case are added beyond the named suites.

rubric.pass: The swapped order times out on a short fuse, the fixed order passes, and the guilty rank is named from evidence.
rubric.strong: A second mismatch class, shape or dtype, is drilled with its distinct symptom.

rubric.pass: Derived byte factors match measured knees on CPU, and every number carries its backend, tier and commit.
rubric.strong: The crossover prediction is tested against a sweep and the residual is attributed.

rubric.pass: The suite is green with deterministic seeds and distinct ports, and the injected fault fails its exact assertion.
rubric.strong: Fault coverage extends to a second class and teardown leaves no orphan holding the port.

miniProject.feedsInto: Rank and group construction plus the collective suite feed data, sharded and model parallel sections and the capstone evidence core.
